- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days) are common; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If 3+ consecutive days of high sentiment (≥ 0.67) followed by price drop, model often fails to correct; apply downward bias in next 5 days.
- Model tends to lag in early days of new sentiment trend; forecast should be adjusted 1–2 days ahead of true price if sentiment shifts sharply.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +0.67), model often misreads momentum; use 3-day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates in high-sentiment periods; apply 1–2% downward correction if sentiment > 0.70 for 5+ consecutive days.
- If true price deviates > 3% from forecast for 2+ consecutive days, check sentiment for reversal signal; adjust forecast to match sentiment direction.
